source_text: The passage referred to, reads as follows: ‘For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy.” This passage, if the holiness of which it speaks signifies church-membership, will prove too much.
claim: 코린토전서 7:14의 성경 구절이 교회 회원 자격을 의미하는 경우에는 너무 많은 것을 증명할 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The word “ sanctified,” which is applied to the unbelieving husband and unbelieving wife, means made holy.
claim: 성경에서 '거룩하게 함'이라는 단어는 믿지 않는 남편과 아내에게 적용되어 그들을 거룩하게 만든다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These unbelievers, therefore, were also holy; and must, according to the interpretation, have been members of the church.
claim: 비신자 남편과 비신자 아내도 거룩한 자들이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The text is a process of reasoning; and the laws of reasoning require, that the term “holy” in the conclusion, should be used in the same sense as in the premises.
claim: 논증의 법칙에 따라 '거룩한'이라는 용어는 결론과 전제에서 동일한 의미로 사용되어야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If holiness implies church-membership, when predicated of the children, it must imply the same when predicated of the unbelieving husband and wife.
claim: 성스러움은 교회 회원 자격을 의미한다면, 아이들에게 적용될 때와 믿지 않는 부부에게 적용될 때 동일한 의미를 가져야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But no one imagines that those unbelievers were members of the church; and, therefore, the holiness affirmed of the children, is not church-membership.
claim: 아이들의 성결은 교회 회원권을 의미하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If it be asked, what holiness could be predicated of these children, or of the unbelieving husband and wife, which did not include church-membership—the answer is at hand.
claim: 어린이나 믿지 않는 부부에게 속한 어떤 종류의 거룩함이 교회 회원권을 포함하지 않는지를 묻는다면 그 답은 가까이에 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The Jewish Christians retained this opinion, as is manifest from Gal. ii. 12.
claim: 유대인 기독교인들은 비유대인들과의 접촉을 부정한 것으로 간주하는 유대인의 의견을 유지했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: According to this opinion, they with whom familiar intercourse was lawful, were considered holy; and all others were unclean.
claim: 유대인 기독교인들은 친밀한 교제가 허용되는 사람들을 거룩한 것으로, 다른 사람들을는 부정한 것으로 여겼다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The question had arisen among the Corinthians, probably from the influence of Judaizing teachers, whether familiar intercourse with unbelievers is lawful.
claim: 코린토인들 사이에 믿지 않는 사람들과의 친밀한 교제가 합법적인지에 대한 질문이 발생했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In the fifth chapter of the epistle, Paul discusses this question, and decides that association in church-membership with such persons, was unlawful; but that ordinary intercourse with them must be admitted, or Christians “‘ must needs go out of the world.” As the principle which he opposed had produced a doubt among the
claim: 교회에서 그런 사람들과의 교제는 불법이지만, 평범한 상호작용은 받아들여야 하며, 그렇지 않으면 기독교인들은 세상을 떠나야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Corinthians, whether it was lawful for Christians to live in familiar intercourse with unbelieving husbands or wives, Paul considers this case in the seventh chapter.
claim: 코린토인들에게 기독교인들이 믿지 않는 배우자와 친밀한 관계를 유지하는 것이 합법적인지에 대한 문제를 바울은 7장에서 다룬다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He decides that, if this principle may disturb the domestic relations, it will separate parent and child, as well as husband and wife.
claim: 바울은 기독교인과 비기독교인 배우자 사이의 가정을 포함한 가정 관계가 교란될 수 있는 원칙에 대해 고려한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If familiar intercourse with the unconverted is unlawful in one case, it is unlawful in the other also.
claim: 하나의 경우에 불신자와의 친밀한 교제가 불법일 경우 다른 경우에도 불법이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But this argument presupposes, that the children, like the unbelieving husband and wife, were not members of the church.
claim: 사도 시대에는 어린 아이들이 교회 회원으로 간주되지 않았다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The text, therefore, furnishes decisive proof, that infant church-membership was unknown in the time of the apostles.!
claim: 아기들의 교회 회원 자격은 사도 시대에는 알려지지 않았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Argument 4.--The writers of the New Testament used words in the sense in which they were accustomed to read them in the Scriptures of the Old Testament.
claim: 신약 성경 저자들은 구약 성경에서 읽어왔던 의미에 따라 단어를 사용했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The Greek word Christ, corresponded to the Hebrew word Messiah; and both words denoted the same person.
claim: 그리스어 단어 Christ는 히브리어 단어 Messiah와 동일한 사람을 가리킨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The Greek word ecclesia, was not a newly-invented term; but it was the word by which the LXX. had rendered the Hebrew eahal, of the Old Testament, and must therefore be understood to denote the same thing, the Congregation of the Lord.
claim: 그리스어 ecclesia는 새로운 용어가 아니며, 구약의 히브리어 eahal을 번역한 LXX의 용어로, 주님의 회衆을 나타낸다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Hence the church was not a new organization.
claim: 교회는 새로운 조직이 아니다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It was the Hebrew congregation, continued under the new dispensation ; and, as children were included with their parents, in the former dispensation, the right of membership cannot now be denied to them.
claim: 교회는 구약의 회중이 새로운 은혜 아래 계속된 것であり, 어린이들은 부모와 함께 포함되어 있었으므로 현재 회원 자격을 거부할 수 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The identity of the church under both dispensations is further apparent in the fact, that the names Zion and Jerusalem, derived from the places where the Old Testament worshippers assembled, are given to the church of the New Testament.
claim: 구약과 신약下的 교회는 동일하다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It is true that the Hebrew word Messiah, and the corresponding Greek word Christ, denoted the same person; but it cannot be hence inferred as a universal truth, that identity, either of person or things, always attends identity or correspondence of name.
claim: 같은 이름이나 호칭이 동일한 사람이나 사물을 의미하는 것은 아님

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The Hebrew name Joshua is applied in Scripture to different persons ;? and the corresponding Greek name Jesus, is applied to persons different from these, and different from one another.?
claim: 성경에서 동일한 이름이 같은 사람이나 사물을 가리키지 않을 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The name Assembly „sometimes signifies the legislative body of a state, and sometimes an ecclesiastical judicatory.
claim: Assembly라는 이름은 때때로 국가의 입법부를 의미하고 때때로 교회 재판을 의미한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: With this name the Hebrew and Greek words for congregation and church very nearly correspond in signification; but were the correspondence perfect, it could not be inferred that organized societies denoted by them must be identical.
claim: 교회와 회중을 나타내는 히브리어와 그리스어 단어가 거의 같은 의미를 가지지만, 완전히 일치한다고 해도 반드시 동일한 조직적인 사회를 의미하는 것은 아님

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But the correspondence between the designations of the church and of the Hebrew congregation is not perfect.
claim: 교회와 히브리어 회중의 명칭 사이에 완전한 상응성은 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If any one should argue from hence, that whenever the New Testament writers use the words xanGos, and cvraywyn, they must mean the Hebrew congregation, he would err egregiously.
claim: 신약 성경 작가들이 'xanGos'와 'cvraywyn'이라는 단어를 사용할 때 항상 히브리 회중을 의미하는 것은 아님

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The argument which would be so fallacious when applied to these words, cannot be valid when applied to exxanova.
claim: 어떤 사람이 'exxanova'에 대한 논증이 유효하다고 주장한다면, 이는 xanGos와 cvraywyn에 적용했을 때의 오류와 같은 잘못된 결론이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The Hebrew congregation was called the Congregation of the Lord or Jehovah, and the Congregation of Israel.
claim: 히브리 회중은 주님 또는 여호와의 회중과 이스라엘의 회중으로 불렸다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It was a congregation instituted for the worship of Jehovah as the God of the Hebrew nation.
claim: 히브리 회중은 여호와를 히브리 민족의 하나님으로 예배하기 위해 설립된 회중이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The church is called the church of God, and the church of Christ.
claim: 교회는 하나님의 교회이자 그리스도의 교회로 불린다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These full designations of the two bodies are by no means coincident; but we have proof that the two bodies are not identical, which is far more to be relied on than a want of coincidence in their names.
claim: 교회와 그리스도의 몸은 동일하지 않다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When the New Testament church is first introduced in the sacred writings, Jesus calls it not the cahal or ecclesia of Israel, but my ecclesia.
claim: 예수님은 새 계명의 교회를 이스라엘의 회衆(cchal)이나 교회(ecclesia)라고 부르지 않고,私の 교회(my ecclesia)라고 불렀다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He moreover speaks of it as yet to be constructed: “ On this rock will I build my ecclesia.” It cannot be that he intended the cahal of Israel which was instituted in the time of Moses, and its organization completed in the most minute particulars.
claim: 예수님은 이스라엘의 회衆(cchal or ecclesia of Israel)이 아닌 자신의 교회(my ecclesia)를 말씀하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: the ecclesia, let him be, &c.’’ Can it be true that the New Testament writer who recorded these words, understood the word ecclesia in the sense in which he had been accustomed to read it in the Scriptures of the Old Testament, as referring to the Hebrew cahal?
claim: 신약 성경 저자가 기록한 'ecclesia'라는 단어는 구약 성경의 'Hebrew cahal'과 같은 의미로 이해했을 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Can it be that Jesus meant it to be so understood?
claim: 예수님은 교회(ecclesia)를 구약 성경의 히브리어 단어 'cahal'과 같은 의미로 이해하셨을 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The next mention of the New Testament ecclesia is equally decisive: “The Lord added to the ecclesia such as should be saved.” The time was the feast of Pentecost, when the worshippers of the Hebrew cahal were assembled at Jerusalem.
claim: 초기 기독교 교회는 구원받을 사람들을 추가하여 성장하였다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: From this assembly the converts to the new religion were made; and when made, they were added to the ecclesia.
claim: 새로운 종교로 개종한 사람들은 교회에 추가되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: No proof more decisive can be desired; that the ecclesia to which they were added, was not the cahal to which they had previously belonged.
claim: 새로 개종한 사람들은 이전에 속해 있던 카할이 아닌 에클레시아에 추가되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When Jesus said, “Tell it to the church;” the Christian churches -in which discipline was to be exercised had not yet been organized.
claim: 예수님이 '교회에 말하라'라고 말씀하셨을 때, 교회紀律이 행해질 기독교 교회들은 아직 조직되지 않았었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The master of the family was still present to manage the affairs of the household by his direct authority; but he gave the command to be observed after his departure, as a perpetual rule of discipline.
claim: 예수님의 교회에 대한 말씀은 아직 조직되지 않은 교회의 규율을 위한 지시였다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The unguarded manner in which he speaks of the ecclesia, furnishes proof of no inconsiderable force, that the word which he employed, was not at the time in familiar use as a name for the congregation of Jewish worshippers.
claim: 예수님이 교회에 대한 명령을 내릴 때 사용한 단어가 당시 유대인 예배자들의 집회를 가리키는 일반적인 용어는 아니었다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Had it been, this application of the word would have been natural to the disciples, and some accompanying explanations would have been needed to guard them from mistake.
claim: 예수님의 제자들에게 교회를 설명할 때, 이미 익숙한 용어를 사용했다면 추가적인 설명이 필요했을 것이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When intending that which did not yet exist, of which they had no personal knowledge, and which never had existed, he would not, without explanation, have employed a term to denote it, with which they were familiar as the name of something that had long existed and was well known to them.
claim: 예수님이 새로운 개념을 설명할 때는 이미 익숙한 용어를 사용하지 않았을 것

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The conclusion to which this argument tends, is strongly corroborated by the fact, that although the word ecclesia occurs in the New Testament more than a hundred times, it never, with but one exception, denotes the people of Israel; and in this single exception, “ He that was in the ecclesia in the wilderness,” ? it does not
claim: 성경에서 'ecclesia'라는 용어가 사용될 때, 대체로 이스라엘 백성을 가리키지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: denote the people of Israel as an enduring organization, but refers _ to a particular time in their history, when they were assembled at Sinai to receive the law, and for this reason it should have been translated assembly.
claim: 이스라엘의 교회는 특정 시기에 모인 공동체를 의미한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: As an enduring body, they are called the house of Israel, the commonwealth of Israel, the people, the nation ; but the ecclesia they are never called.
claim: 이스라엘의 영속적인 집단은 여러 이름으로 불리지만, 교회(ecclesia)라고는 절대 불리지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The passage, “In the midst of the ecclesia I will sing praise unto thee,” ' is quoted from the Old Testament, where the word cahal is used, and where there is an allusion to the Hebrew congregation; but as used by Paul, the ecclesia intended consists of the “many sons” brought to glory, who are mentioned in the context.
claim: 바울이 말하는 교회는 영광에 이르게 된 많은 아들들로 구성된 공동체이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The same ecclesia is afterwards spoken of, “ The church of the first born,” with an apparent allusion to the assembly of Old Testament worshippers.
claim: 바울이 말하는 교회는 영광에 이르게 된 많은 아들들로 구성된 교회이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This allusion may be readily accounted for by the fact, that the worship of the Old Testament dispensation was “a shadow of good things to come.” Zion and Jerusalem were types of heaven, the future meeting place of the saints; and the congregation of Israel assembled for the worship of God, typified that future assembly in which the redeemed of the Lord shall come from the east, the west, the north, and the south, and shall sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of Heaven.
claim: 구약의 예배는 미래에 올 좋은 것들의 그림자였으며, 시온과 예루살렘은 천국을 상징하는 표상이었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This fully accounts for the use which the prophets have made of the names Zion and Jerusalem, in predicting the glory of the church.
claim: 예언자들은 교회의 영광을 예언할 때 시온과 예루살렘의 이름을 사용하였다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The Hebrew cahal was an actual assembly.
claim: 히브리어로 'cahal'는 실제 모임을 의미한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Three times in the year the tribes were required to meet for public worship in the place where the Lord would put his name.?
claim: 이스라엘의 지파들은 매년 세 번씩 주님께서 이름을 두신 곳에서 공적 예배를 위해 모여야 했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This obligation continued as long as the ordinances of their worship were obligatory; and ceased when the handwriting of them was nailed to the cross of Christ.
claim: 구약의 예배 규례는 그리스도의 십자가에 못 박혀 더 이상 의무가 아님을 의미한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: An intimation that the obligation to meet at Jerusalem was to cease, is given in the words of Christ to the women of Samaria: “The hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.’”’?
claim: 예루살렘에서 예배하는 의무는 그리스도의 십자가에 못 박히면서 끝났음이 시마리아 여인들에게 주신 말씀을 통해 암시됨

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When men were no longer required to meet in Jerusalem, the cahal of Israel was dissolved.
claim: 예루살렘에서 모이는 의무가 더 이상 요구되지 않게 되면서 이스라엘의 회衆은 해산되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Although, in the divine purpose, a sufficient sacrifice for sin had been provided from eternity, yet it did not seem good to Infinite Wisdom that it should be immediately offered, when sin first entered into the world.
claim: 하나님의 계획에서 죄에 대한 충분한 제사는 영원 전부터 제공되었지만, 하나님은 처음으로 죄가 세상에 들어왔을 때 즉시 그것을 제공하는 것이 좋지 않다고 생각했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Four thousand years of ignorance and crime, God winked at, or overlooked as unworthy of his regard, or unfit for his purpose; and fixed his eyes on that period denominated “the fulness of time,” when it would best display the divine perfections, for the Redeemer to atone for transgression; and repentance and remission of sins to be preached in his name, among all nations.
claim: 하나님의 지혜는 인간의 죄를 즉시 용서하지 않으시고, 오히려 약 4000년 동안 기다리신 후에야 구속자의 죽음과 죄 사함을 모든 민족에게 선포하시는 적절한 때가 되어서야 그들을 용서하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: As, in the exercises of an individual Christian, the discovery of salvation in Christ is withheld, until an anxiety is excited in his breast that makes the discovery welcome; so in the history of the world, the Messiah makes not his appearance, until mankind have felt the necessity of such a deliverer; then he comes, the desire of all nations.
claim: 구원者の 필요성을 인식한 후에 메시야가 나타난다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It pleased God that a full experiment should be made of man’s power and skill to find a remedy for his moral disease, before God’s remedy for the healing of the nations should be revealed and applied.
claim: 하나님은 인간이 자신의 도덕적 병을 치료하기 위해 모든 능력과 지혜를 다 사용해 보기 전에, 하나님의 구원 계획을 계시하지 않으셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: “ After that, in the wisdom of God, the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God, by the foolishness of preaching, to save them that believe.”
claim: 하나님은 세상의 지혜로 하나님을 알지 못하는 세계에서, 설교의 어리석음으로 믿는 자들을 구원하기를 기뻐하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The experiment which, in the wisdom of God, opened the way for the Redeemer’s entrance into the world, was of a two-fold nature; or, rather, there were two distinct experiments, demonstrating distinet truths.
claim: 하나님의 지혜에 따라 구세주가 세상을 들어올 수 있도록 한 실험은 두 가지 종류의 성격을 가지고 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When the bolder enemies of God and religion make their appeal from the volume of inspiration to the volume of nature, and assert the sufficiency of the latter to enlighten and direct them in the search after God; we can refer to actual experiment, to ascertain how far fallen man, without the oracles of God, can advance toward the knowledge of the Divine character.
claim: 인간은 성경의 계시에 의지하지 않고 자연만으로는 하나님의 본질에 대한 지식을 얻을 수 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: With the light of nature, the bright beams of science, and the keen eye of natural genius, the wisest men of antiquity still felt in the dark, after the unknown God.
claim: 인간은 자연의 빛만으로는 하나님의 본질을 알 수 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When those who profess to receive the truth, deny the doctrine of grace, and maintain that man has sufficient native virtue, if properly cultivated, to render him acceptable to God; that there are
claim: 인간은 타고난 미덕을 제대로 계발하면 하나님께 받아들여질 수 있다고 주장하며, 은혜의 교리를 부정하는 것은 잘못이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: influences of the Word or Spirit common to all men, which arọ Sufficient, without any additional special influence, to bring him to know and enjoy the Most High; we have in the wisdom of God, another completed experiment, which decides against this doctrine, with as much certainty as is anywhere to be found within the limits of experimental philosophy.
claim: 하나님의 지혜는 모든 사람에게 공통된 말씀이나 성령의 영향이 충분하여 추가적인 특별한 영향 없이 가장 높은 것을 알게 하고 즐기도록 할 수 있다는 교리를 반대한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: They were not left to read the volume of nature only ; but to them were committed the oracles of God.
claim: 하나님의 말씀을 읽는 특권이 그들에게 주어졌으며, 이는 자연의 책만 읽는 것과는 다르다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: They were not left with unmeaning forms, and unauthorized rites of religion ; but they had ordinances of divine service, instituted on the authority of God.
claim: 하나님은 그의 백성들에게 의미 있는 종교 형식과 하나님의 권위에 따른 예배의 규례를 주셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: “To them pertained the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises.” Nor were they without instructors in religion ; but holy men were raised up among them, who spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.
claim: 구약의 이스라엘 백성은 하나님의 권위에 따른 예배와 제도, 그리고 성령의 감동을 받은 거룩한 인도를 통해 종교적 지침을 받았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Neither were they without motives to obedience; but a covenant was made with them, containing every threat which might deter—every promise that might allure.
claim: 이스라엘은 하나님과의 언약을 통해 복종할 동기와 이유를 가졌다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It was clearly demonstrated that man is totally depraved; that the best institutions, instructions, and motives, with all common influences of the Spirit, whatever such there may be, are altogether insufficient to restore his fallen nature; and that a direct special influence upon his heart, by the effectual working of Divine power, is indispensably necessary, in order to make him delight in the law of God, and render acceptable obedience to its holy requirements.
claim: 인간은 전적으로 타락하여 神의 법을 기뻐하고 그 거룩한 요구에 순종하기 위해서는 인간의 마음에 대한 直接적인 特殊한 영향이 필요하다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: That society of persons which was the subject of the last-mentioned experiment, is frequently denominated the Congregation of the Lord.
claim: 주님의 회중이라고 불리는 그 사회는 종종 언급된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It appears to have been the orly divinely instituted society, organized for religious worship, that ever existed before the coming of Christ.
claim: 그리스도 이전에 존재한 유일한 신적으로 제정된 종교적 예배를 위한 사회는 하나님의 회衆이었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: That God designed by the Mosaic dispensation, of which this congregation was the subject, to give a clear demonstration of man’s depravity, may be inferred from the end which has actually been accomplished, and from such declarations of Scripture as the following: “ The law was added because of transgression until the seed should come.
claim: 모세의 계시에 의한 하나님의 목적은 인간의 타락을 분명히 보여주기 위한 것이었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: the offence might abound.” Since unto God all his works from the beginning are known, he well knew the imperfections of the Mosaic covenant, even from the time of its institution, and what would be the result of the experiment.
claim: 하나님은 모세의 언약이 제대로 작동하지 않는다는 것을 이미 알고 있었고, 그것을 더 좋은 언약으로 대체할 계획을 세웠다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He found fault with it long before its abrogation ; and so prepared it at first, that it typified and foretold a better covenant that should succeed it, established upon better promises.
claim: 하나님은 모세의 언약이 제대로 작동하지 않는다는 것을 이미 알고 있었으며, 그것을 더 좋은 언약으로 대체할 계획을 세웠다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The first account that the Scriptures give of the Congregation of the Lord, we find in the twelfth chapter of Exodus.
claim: 성경에서 주님의 회중에 대한 첫 번째 설명은 출애굽기 12장에서 찾을 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When a new order of things was introduced ; when the year received a new beginning, and became, as it has been called, the ecclesiastical year; when God took his people by the hand, to lead them out of the land of Egypt;! when that code of laws for the regulation of religious worship, which the apostle means by the first covenant throughout his epistle to the Hebrews, began to be promulgated ; and the Passover, as one of the ordinances of divine service pertaining to the first covenant, was instituted; then, first, are the Israelites recognised as a worshipping congregation.
claim: 이스라엘 백성이 하나님의 인도하심을 받으며 출애굽의 여정에서 새로운 규례와 예배의식을 시작하면서 처음으로 하나님께서는 이스라엘 백성을 예배하는 공동체로 인정하였다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Before this, the word of the Lord had come to individuals, and individuals had performed religious rites; but now, the word is sent to a whole congregation, and that congregation, by divine appointment, perform a rite of divine worship simultaneously.
claim: 이스라엘 백성은 하나님의 말씀을 받고 예배 의식을 수행한 개인들에서 예배하는 공동체로 발전했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Before this, the Israelites had indeed been distinguished from the rest of mankind; but not by the characteristics of a worshipping society.
claim: 이스라엘인들은 이전에 다른 사람들과는 구별되었지만, 예배하는 사회의 특징으로는 구별되지 않았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: That there were persons among them who worshipped God in sincerity and truth, will not be disputed.
claim: 이스라엘 사람들 중에 하나님을 진심과 진리대로 경배하는 사람들이 있었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Where their statute book, the laws of their worship, the rules of their society, &c.?
claim: 하나님의 말씀에 따라 규정된 예배의 형식과 의식이 없는 경우, 하나님은 그 사회를 구성하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: A worshipping society, without forms, and rites, and rules of worship, God never constituted.
claim: 하나님은 형식과 의식 및 예배 규칙이 없는 예배 사회를 결성한 적이 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The seed of Abraham were destined to be the subjects of special dispensations, throughout all their generations.
claim: 아브라함의 자손은 모든 세대에 걸쳐 특별한 섭리의 대상이 될 운명에 놓여 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But, during all this intermediate time, they were the subjects of that peculiar, experimental, preparatory dispensation, which we a i ne ea a 5
claim: 이스라엘은 중간 기간 동안 특별한 실험적이고 준비적인 섭리를 받았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: They were constituted, and continued to be, the Lord’s peculiar cahal, his only worshipping congregation.
claim: 이스라엘은 주님의 특별한 회衆으로서 계속 존재했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But while the ordinances of. their worship were wisely contrived to be types and prophecies of Christ, at the same time that they afforded to the world that experiment, which appears to have been so important a part of their design; in like manner, an instructive intimation of the future exclusion of the Jews from gospel privileges, and of the admission of the gentiles, appears to have been given, in the character of the members who composed this sacred congregation.
claim: 구약의 예배 규례는 그리스도를預표하고 예언하는 것이었으며, 동시에 유대인들이 복음 특권에서 제외되고 이방인들이 받아들여지는 미래를 암시했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The great body of its constituents were the descendants of Abraham; but provision was made in its charter, that Israelites in some cases should be excluded, and that gentiles might be admitted.?
claim: 이스라엘의 성회는 아브라함의 자손들로 구성되었지만 이스라엘인บาง 경우에는 제외되고 외인들이 받아들여질 수 있도록 규정되어 있었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Nothing like this can be found in the covenant made with Abraham and his seed, as recorded in the 17th chapter of Genesis.
claim: 아브라함과 그의 자손에게 주어진 언약에는 이스라엘인과 이방인의 구별이 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This covenant received into its arms every circumcised son of Jacob (in whom the seed was ultimately called), without any exception ; and thrust from its embrace every Gentile, without any distinction.
claim: 야곱의 자손 중 할례를 받은 모든 아들을 예외 없이 받아들이고, 이방인은 구별 없이 배척하는 약속이 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It was, indeed, one of its stipulations that every Israelite should have all the males of his house circumcised; but there is no intimation that they were all thereby incorporated among the covenant seed, or that they had more right to the territory granted in the covenant, than had Ishmael, or the sons of Keturah.
claim: 유대인의 할례는 언약의 특권을 자동으로 부여하지 않는다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Jacob’s servants were circumcised ; but they did not become heads of tribes in Israel, as they would have been, had circumcision endowed them with the privileges of the covenant seed.
claim: 약식은 언약의 특권을 자동으로 부여하지 않는다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When the end for which any society was instituted has been accomplished, it is natural to expect its dissolution.
claim: 어떤 사회가 그 목적을 달성하면 해산되는 것이 자연스럽다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The experiment for which the Congregation of the Lord had been organized, was completely made, when the Redeemer appeared, in the end of the world, “to take away sin by the sacrifice of himself.” The first covenant, established upon conditional promises, was proved, upon due trial, to be faulty, weak, and.unprofitable ; and the necessity of a better covenant, whose better promises should be all yea and amen in Christ Jesus, was clearly demonstrated: “ He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” When “There was a disannulling of the commandment going before,” in which was contained the charter of the Congregation of the Lord, the
claim: 구원者の 출현과 제사의 통해 첫 번째 언약이 불완전하여 새로운 언약의 필요성이 입증되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Deprived of the character of a worshipping congregation, it lost its existence.
claim: 예배하는 공동체의 특성을 잃으면 존재 자체를 잃는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The wall that had enclosed it from the rest of mankind, was broken down, when its ordinances were nailed to the cross of Christ."
claim: 그리스도님의 십자가에 의해서 교회의 규례가 폐지됨으로써 교회와 세상을 구분짓던 장벽이 무너졌다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: We have not insisted on the obvious difference between the church and the Hebrew congregation, as to the character of the members composing them.
claim: 교회와 히브리 회중은 구성원들의 특성에 있어 명백한 차이가 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The congregation consisted mainly of Israelites; and these were admitted without regard to moral character, if circumcised, and free from ceremonial defilement and bodily defect.
claim: 히브리 회중은 출생이나 할례와 같은 요건에 따라 구성원들이 가입되었으며, 도덕적 品格은 고려되지 않았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Gentiles were admitted, on conforming to the law of circumcision; but a Moabite, or Ammonite, could not be admitted until the tenth generation; and the most pious Israelite was prohibited, if he was-ceremonially defiled, or the subject of a particular bodily defect.?
claim: 유대인 회중은 율법의 규례에 따라 순종과 제사 불결, 신체 결함 없이 할례를 받은 이들을 받아들이며, ngoại인들은 할례를 받고, 모압인이나 암몬인은 10세代까지 받아들여지지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In Christ Jesus, circumcision availeth nothing, but a new creature.
claim: 그리스도 예수 안에서 할례는 아무 소용이 없지만 새 피조물이 됩니다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Moabites and Ammonites are not excluded; but, in every nation, he that feareth God, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.* Ceremonial defilement and bodily defects constitute no obstacle to the fellowship of the saints.
claim: 모압인과 암몬인은 배제되지 않으며, 모든 민족에서 하나님을 경외하고 의를 행하는 자는 그 앞에서 받아들여진다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If the institution were the same, such radical changes in the membership could not well consist with the continued membership of infants.
claim: 같은 제도가 유지된다면, 회원 구성의 이러한 급격한 변화는 어린아이들의 계속적인 회원資格과 잘 일치하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But the Mosaic institution has been abolished: “ For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before, for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” * ‘For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.”*® ‘He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” 6
claim: 모세의 제도는 폐지되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Some advocates of infant church-membership, admit the temporary nature of the Mosaic institution; but maintain that there ran through it, and was contained in it, a spiritual and unchangeable covenant, which had been made with Abraham, and which is now in force.
claim: 어린아이 교회 회원권을 주장하는 일부 사람들은 모세의 제도가 일시적이라는 것을 인정하지만, 아브라함과 맺은 영적이고 불변하는 계약이 그 안에 포함되어 있었고 지금도 시행되고 있다고 주장한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Argument 5.—The Lord promised Abraham, that in him all nations of the earth should be blessed; and entered into a covenant with him, constituting him the father of many nations, and engaging to be the God of him and his seed.
claim: 하나님은 아브라함에게 모든 민족을 축복하도록 약속하시고, 그를 많은 나라의 아버지로 삼으시며, 그와 그의 자손의 하나님이 되심을 언약으로 맺으셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Believers in all nations where the gospel is preached, are accounted the children of Abraham;
claim: 복음이 전파되는 모든 민족에서 믿는 자들은 아브라함의 자녀로 여겨진다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: and admitted into this covenant, and become members of God’s church.
claim: 하나님의 교회에 속한 사람들은 하나님과의 언약에 참여하며 그 안에서 회원이 된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In this covenant, children have always been included With their parents; and their right to its privileges was recognised by Peter, on the day of Pentecost, in these words: “ The promise is to you and your children.” That believing gentiles were received into the same covenant which belonged to national Israel, is taught by these words of Christ: “ The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.” 1 And still more clearly by Paul, under the figure of the good olive-tree, of which the people of Israel were the natural branches; but into which believing gentiles were grafted, so as to partake of the root and fatness of the olive-tree.
claim: 子供들은 부모와 함께 언약에 포함되어 왔으며, 그들의 특권에 대한 권리는 베드로가 오순절 날에 말한 이 말씀으로 인식되었다: "약속은 너와 네 자녀에게로다."

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In this way, the blessing of Abraham comes on the gentiles; and the covenant which secures the blessing, embraces their children with them.
claim: 아브라함의 축복이 이방인에게 오고, 그 축복을 보장하는 계약은 그들의 자녀들을 포함한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: “Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will show thee: and I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing; and I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee; and in thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed.”’?
claim: 하나님은 아브람에게 그의 조상 집과 친척을 떠나 하나님이 보여줄 땅으로 가라고 명령하시고, 그를 통해 큰 민족을 만들고 축복하며, 그의 이름을 위대하게 하시고, 모든 족속이 그로 말미암아 복을 받도록 하신다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In this narrative, all is to be taken literally.
claim: 이 성경 기록은 문자 그대로 받아들여야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The command was meant, and understood, and obeyed, according to the literal import of the words.
claim: 명령은 문자적인 의미로 이해되고 순종되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The promise has thus far been fulfilled in its literal sense, and is still in progress of literal accomplishment.
claim: 하나님의 약속은 문자적인 의미에서 지금까지 성취되었으며 여전히 진행 중이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Abraham was personally blessed with eminent piety, and extraordinary tokens of the Divine favor.
claim: 아브라함은 개인적으로 두드러진 경건과 특별한 하나님의 은혜의 표징으로 축복을 받았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The nation of Israel, descended from him, was great in number, and strength, and great in its influence on the world.
claim: 아브라함의 후손인 이스라엘 민족은 수와 힘, 그리고 세계에 미치는 영향력이 크다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: To this nation, under God, mankind are indebted for the Bible, the gospel; and, above all, the Saviour of the world, who was, according to the flesh, of the seed of Abraham.
claim: 인류는 이스라엘 민족에게 성경, 복음, 그리고 세상의 구원자를 빚지고 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This nation has given to the world the knowledge of the true God; which knowledge is ultimately to overspread the earth, and bless all nations.
claim: 이 민족은 세계에 참된 하나님에 대한 지식을 주었으며, 이 지식은 궁극적으로 온 땅을 덮치고 모든 민족을 축복할 것이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: pronuse made to Abraham, that in him all the families of the earth should be blessed, will be fulfilled.
claim: 아브라함에게 하신 약속이 성취될 것

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This promise was repeated to the patriarch, after the birth of his son Isaac, in these words: “ And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.’’?
claim: 아브라함에게 하신 약속이 그의 아들 이삭의 출생 후에 반복되었고, 모든 민족이 그의 씨를 통해 복을 받게 될 것이라고 말씀하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The source of blessing to mankind was originally in the person of Abraham, but was now transferred to the person of the son that had been born of him: and hence the language of the promise was changed, “In thy seed,” &c.
claim: 아브라함에게 주어진 축복의 근원은 원래 아브라함 자신에게 있었지만, 이제 그의 아들 이삭에게로 옮겨졌고, 그 결과 약속의 언어는 '너의 씨'라고 바뀌었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The same promise was afterwards repeated to Isaac,” and to Jacob.* This promise is frequently referred to in the Scriptures, and is called the covenant which God made with the fathers*—the word covenant being used according to its latitude of meaning, to denote a firm and stable promise; and it is once called, the gospel preached unto Abraham.
claim: 하나님의 약속이 아브라함에게서 그의 아들 Isaac과 Jacob에게로 전해졌으며 이 약속은 성경에서 자주 언급되며 아버지们との 계약으로 불린다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: No doubt can exist, that this important and distinguished promise included spiritual blessings; but the language is not spiritual in the sense in which this epithet is sometimes used, to mark what is not literal.
claim: 아브라함에게 하신 약속은 영적 축복을 포함한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Every word of this ‘gospel to Abraham,” is as literal as the gospel declaration of Paul: “ Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.”
claim: 아브라함에게 주어진 복음은 문자적으로 이해되어야 하며, 바울의 복음 선언과 마찬가지로 영적인 축복을 포함한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: “ And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them; and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
claim: 하나님은 아브라함에게 그의 자손이 하늘의 별과 같이 많을 것이라고 약속하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.” ê
claim: 아브라함이 주를 믿었으며 그것을 그의 의로 여겼다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Here, again, all is to be understood in the literal sense.
claim: 성경의 내용은 문자적인 의미로 이해되어야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The posterity promised to the patriarch, were literal descendants, persons born out of his bowels.” The great blessing of justification, bestowed on this eminent believer, is spiritual in its nature; but the language in which it is described, is as simple and literal as that which is used in the New Testament, to denote the same blessing: “ By him, all that believe are justified from all things.”
claim: 아브라함에게 약속된 자손은 그의 실제 후손이며, 의롭다 함을 받는 큰 복음은 영적인 본질이지만 그 설명에 사용된 언어는 신약에서 같은 복음을 나타내는 것과 같이 단순하고 문자적이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The third event which claims our consideration, gave existence to the covenant of circumcision.
claim: 할례의 언약이 존재하게 된 세 번째 사건을 고려해야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: appeared to Abram, and said unto him: I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.
claim: 하나님은 아브람에게 나타나서 자기 앞에서 완전하게 행하라고 명령했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly.
claim: 하나님은 아브람과 언약을 맺고 그를极도로 번성하게 하시겠다고 약속하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: And Abram fell on his face, and God talked with him, saying, As for me, behold my covenant is with thee.”
claim: 하나님은 아브람과 언약을 맺으시고 그에게 말씀하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This has been supposed by some, to be more than was true of Abraham, in the literal sense; but they err.
claim: 아브라함에 대한 어떤 사람들의 가정은 사실이 아님

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: From Ishmael, the son of Abraham by Hagar, twelve nations were descended.!
claim: 아브라함의 아들 이스마엘은 하갈을 통해 12개의 국가를 낳았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: No reason, therefore, exists for abandoning the literal sense of the clause.
claim: 아브라함의 자손에 대한 구절을 문자적으로 이해할 이유가 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: We have no right to insist on such a sense for the word “nation,” as will correspond with its use in modern history.
claim: 성경의 단어 'nation'에 대한 의미는 현대 역사에서의 사용과 일치하지 않을 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: What it meant, when the covenant was made, is what it means in this clause; and in this sense, the promise has been literally fulfilled.
claim: 성약이 체결되었을 때 'nation'이라는 단어가 의미하는 바가 이 조항에서 의미하는 바이며, 이러한 의미에서 약속은 문자 그대로 이루어졌다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The change was doubtless significant; but the supposition that it had any signification which militates against the literal construction of the covenant, is wholly unfounded.
claim: 아브라함의 이름 변경은 언약에 대한 문자적인 해석과는 무관하다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The posterity of the patriarch, including the many inspired prophets whom God raised up among them, the first preachers of the gospel, and the writers of the New Testament, were accustomed to use this new name Abraham to signify their literal ancestor.
claim: 아브라함의 후손들은 아브라함을 문자적으로 조상으로 여겼다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It was not in some mystical sense that God made him exceedingly fruitful; and, therefore, the phrase, “I have made thee a father of nations,” does not need a mystical interpretation.
claim: 하나님께서 아브라함을 果實豊かな 존재로 만든 것은 신비적인 의미가 아니라 실제로 그의 자손을 번성시킴으로써 이루어진 것이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: God “made Abraham fruitful,” not by some mystical appointment, but by literally multiplying his seed; and in this literal sense he made him the father of many nations.
claim: 하나님은 아브라함에게 실제로 그의 자손을 번성하게 하심으로써 그를 많은 민족의 아버지로 삼으셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The promise, “and kings shall come out of thee,” was literally fulfilled; and this clause, a mystical interpretation of which no one has ventured to insist on, binds down the covenant to the literal construction.
claim: 하나님의 약속은 아브라함에게 왕들이 나올 것이라는 것이 문자적으로 이루어졌으며, 이 약속은 언약을 문자적 해석에 묶어 놓았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: A difficulty would attend the interpretation, if the term “ everlasting” always denoted unlimited duration; but this was not its only signification.
claim: 영원한이라는 용어는 항상 무제한의 지속을 의미하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The grant of the land of Canaan afterwards made in the covenant, could not extend beyond the duration of the present world; and, if the covenant was to continue in force to the end of time, or even till that state of things should cease, for which the covenant was designed to provide, the epithet “ everlasting” was properly applied to it.
claim: 언약의 기간이 현재 세계의 지속期間을 넘어서지 않는다는 것과 언약이 그 목적으로 설계된 상태가 끝날 때까지 또는 시간의 종말까지 계속 시행될 경우 '영원한'이라는 용어가 적절히 적용됨

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These words were not designed to be a promise of spiritual grace, or eternal life, to all the descendants of Abraham.
claim: 아브라함의 자손들에게 영적 은혜나 영생에 대한 약속이 주어지지 않았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: A new covenant predicted by the prophet Jeremiah, contained the stipulation: “I will be their God; and they shall be my people.” 1 This promise secured spiritual grace; but it would not have been a new covenant if the same grant had been made in the covenant with Abraham.
claim: 예레미야 선지자가 예언한 새로운 언약은 '나는 그들의 하나님이 되고, 그들은 나의 백성이 될 것이다'라는 약속을 포함하며, 이 약속은 영적 은혜를 보장한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: As contained in this covenant, the promise engaged a special divine care over Abraham and his descendants ; and particularly over the nation of Israel, the seed to whom the grant of center a et BRETT a is a)
claim: 아브라함과 그의 자손, 특히 이스라엘 민족에게는 특별한 신적 보호가 약속되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Canaan was made in this covenant.
claim: 가나안은 이 언약에서 창조되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He separated them from all other nations, and acknowledged them to be his people: “ You only have I known of all the families of the earth.” !
claim: 하나님은 이스라엘을 다른 모든 민족과 분리하시고 그들을 그의 백성으로 인정하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: His providence over them, and his revelations to them, were all peculiar, In all his dealings with them, he acted in the relation of a God.
claim: 하나님의 섭리는 이스라엘民族에게 특별하게 나타났으며, 하나님은 그들과의 모든 상호작용에서 하나님의 관계를 유지했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He rewarded as a God, and punished as a God.
claim: 하나님은 그의 백성에게 보상과 징계를 내릴 때 하나님의 지위에서 행동하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He made himself known to them as a God, while other nations were permitted to remain in ignorance of him; and as a God, while he granted to this nation means of grace and salvation unknown to the rest of the world, he used the nation as the channel for conveying spiritual blessings to all the nations of the earth.
claim: 하나님은 특정 민족에게는 은혜와 구원을 주시면서 다른 민족들은 무지하게 두셨고, 이 민족을 통해 모든 민족에게 영적 축복을 전달하는 통로로 사용하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: All this was meant literally, and was literally fulfilled.
claim: 모든 것이 문자적으로 의미되었으며 실제로 이루어졌다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The import of the word “ everlasting,” has been explained in the remarks on the phrase “everlasting covenant.” Whether the word everlasting, either in application to the covenant or to the possession of Canaan, was limited to the dispensation that preceded the time of Christ, or extended into the present dispensation, and still stretches forward into future time, will be a subject of future inquiry.
claim: 구약의 언약과 가나안 영토 소유에 대한 "영원한"이라는 단어의 의미는 그 적용 범위가 예수 그리스도 이전 시대에만 국한되었는지 아니면 현재와 미래에도 계속되는지에 대해 추후 조사할 문제이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But whatever may be true on this question, the use of the word militates nothing against the literal construction of the covenant.
claim: 언약의 문자적 해석에 반대되는 내용은 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: “And God said unto Abraham, thou shalt keep my covenant therefore, thou and thy seed after thee in their generations.
claim: 하나님은 아브라함과 그의 자손에게 언약을 지키라고 명하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you, and thy seed after thee; every man child among you shall be circumcised.
claim: 하나님은 아브라함과 그의 자손에게 할례를 명하셨다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.
claim: 할례는 하나님과 아브라함 및 그의 자손 사이의 언약의 표징이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you; every man child in your generations, he that is born in the house or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of thy seed.
claim: 남자 아이들은 8일이 되면 할례를 받아야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: in thy house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needs be circumcised; and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
claim: 할례는 영적 언약의 상징으로서 중요하며, 이를 지키지 않는 자는 하나님의 백성에서 끊어질 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.”
claim: 할례를 받지 않은 자는 하나님의 언약을 깨뜨린 것으로 간주되어 그의 백성 중에서 끊어질 것이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The precept enjoining circumcision was intended to be understood literally, and it was understood and obeyed literally.
claim: 할례에 관한 계명은 문자적으로 이해되고 지켜져야 했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: An important, very important part of God’s design in making this covenant, was to distinguish and separate the descendants of Abraham from the rest of mankind; and this design would have been frustrated if this part of the covenant had not been taken literally.
claim: 하나님의 언약에서 할례는 아브라함의 자손을 다른 사람들과 구별하기 위한 것이었고, 이것이 문자적으로 이해되고 지켜지지 않았다면 이 목적은 좌절되었을 것이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The whole history of the Hebrew nation, and almost every page of the New Testament, testify in favor of the literal construction.
claim: 성경의 역사와 신약의 거의 모든 페이지가 약속의 문자적 해석을 증거한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The new name Sarah, like the new name Abraham, was significant; but neither of them signified anything contrary to the literal construction of the covenant.
claim: 아브라함과 사라의 새로운 이름은 언약에 대한 문자적인 해석과 모순되지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Abraham was the father of many nations, because he had sons by other wives; but his only son by Sarah was Isaac, the father of Jacob and Esau; and the only nations descended from Sarah, were the Israelites and the Edomites.
claim: 아브라함은 여러 아내에게서 아들을 낳았기 때문에 많은 민족들의 아버지였지만, 사라에게서는 이삭만을 낳았고, 이삭은 야곱과 에서의 아버지가 되었으며, 사라로부터 난 민족은 이스라엘인과 에돔인뿐이었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It was promised that Sarah should be a mother of “ nations,” not of “many nations;” and this adaptation of the ‘language to what became literally true, proves that the covenant was made in the literal sense of the words.
claim: 하나님의 약속은 사라가 여러 민족의 어머니가 될 것이라는 것이 아니라, 하나의 민족을 낳는다는 것으로서 이는 문자적인 의미에서 이루어졌음을 보여준다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In the literal sense kings came out of Sarah; the kings of Edom, and the long line of kings in Israel and Judah.
claim: 사라에서 왕들이 실제로 나왔으며, 에돔의 왕들과 이스라엘과 유다의 장대한 왕들의 계보를 통해 약속이 이루어졌다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Our examination of the covenant has proved conclusively, that it was designed to be understood literally; but a question arises whether it does not admit another and more spiritual sense.
claim: 성약은 문자적으로 이해되도록 설계되었지만 더 영적인 의미를 가질 수도 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The precepts which enjoined the ceremonies of worship to be observed by the Hebrew congregation, were all designed to be understood and obeyed literally.
claim: 히브리 회중이 예배 의식에 대한 규칙을 이해하고 지키도록 명한 모든 계명은 문자적으로 이해되고 지켜지도록 설계되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Literal bulls and goats were to be sacrificed; literal fire was to be used, and all the directions given were to be observed in their literal import.
claim: 히브리 회중의 예배 의식 관행은 문자적으로 이해되고 지켜져야 했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: ceremonies of this worship were shadows of things to come; and a large part of the epistle to the Hebrews is employed in explaining their spiritual signification.
claim: 구약의 예배 의식은 장래에 있을 일들의 그림자였으며, 히브리서에서 그 영적 의미를 설명하는 데 많은 부분이 사용된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Persons and events of the Old Testament which appear in their proper connection as subjects of literal history, are in the New Testament made to represent spiritual things, and spiritual instruction is drawn from them.
claim: 구약의 인물과 사건은 신약에서 영적 의미를 대표하는 것으로 사용된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The history of Hagar, as given in the book of Genesis, is literally true ; but Paul calls it an allegory, and uses it to represent spiritual things.
claim: 성경의 구약 인물과 사건은 그 역사적 맥락에서 문자적으로 이해되지만, 신약에서는 영적인 교훈을 위한 상징으로 사용된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In the same manner the covenant of circumcision is made a source of spiritual instruction.
claim: 할례의 언약은 영적 교훈의 근원으로 사용된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The chief particulars in the covenant which are made representatives of spiritual things, are three:
claim: 할례의 언약은 세 가지 주요한 부분을 통해 영적 것들의 대표자로 만든다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The literal descendants of Abraham are made to represent believers, who are called his children in a different sense of the word.
claim: 아브라함의 실제 자손은 다른 의미에서 그의 자녀라고 불리는 믿는 이를 대표한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The metaphorical use of the terms which denote the paternal and filial relations, is frequent in the Scriptures.
claim: 성경에서 부자 관계를 나타내는 용어들은 비유적으로 자주 사용된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: One who appears at the head of a class of persons as a father appears at the head of his family or tribe, is called the father of that class; and the individuals composing the class, are called his children.
claim: 성경에서 아버지와 자식의 관계를 나타내는 용어들은 종종 비유적으로 사용되며, 어떤 집단이나 계층의 대표자나 창시자는 그 집단의 아버지로 불리며, 해당 집단의 구성원들은 그의 자녀들로 불린다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These persons called fathers, were inventors of arts; and the class of persons who practise these arts are regarded as their children.
claim: 성경에서 '아버지'라고 불리는 사람들은 예술의 발명가들이었으며, 이러한 예술을 실천하는 사람들은 그들의 자녀로 간주된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: So those who practise the piety of which Abraham was an illustrious example, and walk in the footsteps of his faith, are called his children.
claim: 아브라함의 신앙을 따르는 사람들은 아브라함의 자녀로 불린다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In this tropical sense of the term, Jesus said to the wicked Jews, “ If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham.”*?
claim: 아브라함의 자녀는 그의 믿음과 행위를 따르는 사람들이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Since the men whom Jesus addressed were children of Abraham in the literal sense, the distinction between the literal and the metaphorical sense is plainly marked; and the latter sense is made to depend on imitation of Abraham in the works for which he was eminent.
claim: 예수님은 아브라함의 자녀가 된다는 것이 실제로 아브라함과 같은 행동을 한다는 것을 의미한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Paul has distinguished between the literal Jew and the metaphorical Jew;* between the children according to the flesh, and the children of promise.4 The latter, he says, “are counted for the seed ;”’ that is, they are accounted the seed of Abraham when the covenant is viewed as an allegory.
claim: 바울은 육체에 따른 자녀와 약속의 자녀를 구분했으며, 후자는 아브라함의 씨로 계산된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Circumcision is made to represent regeneration, the spiritual change by which men become new creatures.
claim: 할례는 재생을 대표하며, 이는 사람들을 새로운 피조물로 만드는 영적 변화이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Hence it is said, “Tn Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision ; but a new creature.’"!
claim: 그리스도 예수 안에서 할례나 불할례는 아무 것도 소용이 없지만 새 피조물임이 중요하다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: A tropical use of the word circumcise to denote a moral change, is found in the Old Testament: “The Lord thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live.”?
claim: 구약에서 순종의 의미로 사용된 '순수'라는 단어는 하나님의 백성이 주님을 전심으로 사랑하기 위해 마음과 영혼이 변화하는 것을 나타낸다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Paul distinguishes between the literal and the spiritual circumcision; thus, ‘‘ Neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh... ..
claim: 바울은 육체의 외적인 할례와 영적 할례를 구분한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter.’”3 This circumcision of the heart is in another passage called the *‘ circumcision of Christ.” While the literal circumcision which marked the literal seed of Abraham avails nothing in Christ Jesus, the spiritual circumcision marks those who belong to Christ, and who are, in the spiritual sense, the seed of Abraham.
claim: 순수한 마음의 할례는 그리스도 안에서 속한 자들을 표시하며, 이는 영적인 의미에서 아브라함의 씨앗이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: “If ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” 5
claim: 그리스도에게 속한 자들은 아브라함의 씨가 되며 약속에 따라 상속자이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Canaan, the land promised to Abraham and his literal seed, is made to represent heaven, the future inheritance of those who have like faith with the patriarch.
claim: 가나안은 아브라함과 그의 실제 자손에게 약속된 땅으로, 천국을 대표하며, 같은 믿음을 가진 사람들의 미래 유산이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Abraham at the command of God left his native country, and sojourned in the land of Canaan ; but though the land was his by promise, he never obtained possession of it.
claim: 아브라함은 하나님의 명령에 따라 그의 고향을 떠나 가나안 땅에서 거주했지만 약속된 땅을 소유하지 못했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Paul makes a spiritual use of this fact: “ Confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
claim: 바울은 아브라함이 가나안 땅을 소유하지 못한 사실을 영적 의미로 사용하였다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly.” The literal Canaan was present to the sight of the patriarch, as a desirable possession secured by covenant to him and his seed; but the eye of his faith was directed to a better country, of which this was but a type.
claim: 믿음의 눈은 더 나은 천국을 향해 있다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: His spiritual seed are like him in faith, and their faith directs its eye to the same heavenly inheritance.
claim: 아브라함의 영적 자손들은 믿음에서 그를 닮았으며, 그들의 믿음은 같은 하늘 상속재를 향해 눈을 돌린다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The allegorical interpretation of the covenant is beautifully harmonious in all its parts.
claim: 언약의 비유적 해석은 모든 부분에서 아름답게 조화롭다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: As he looked beyond the earthly possession granted to him, and sought a heavenly inheritance, so do they.
claim: 믿는 사람들은 땅의 소유를 넘어서 하늘의 유업을 찾고 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The spiritual truths which the covenant represents in its allegorical use, were not brought into existence by the covenant, and are not dependent on it.
claim: 성약이 상징적으로 사용될 때 나타나는 영적 진리는 성약에 의해 창조되지 않았으며, 그것에 의존하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: They are above it, as the things which the Mosaic ceremonies typified are superior to the ceremonies ; or as a substance is superior to its shadow, and independent of it.
claim: 성약이 상징적으로 사용될 때 나타나는 영적 진리는 성약에 의해 창조되지 않았으며, 그것에 의존하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In the third chapter of Galatians, Paul teaches that believers are the children of Abraham, and are blessed with him ; and he dates back their connection with him to a time that preceded the covenant of circumcision.
claim: 갈라디아인 3장에서 바울은 믿는 자들이 아브라함의 자녀이며 그를 통해 축복을 받으며, 할례의 언약 이전으로 그들의 연관성을 추적한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He says, that “the law was four hundred and thirty years after.” Now, reckoning back four hundred and thirty years from the giving of the law, we arrive at the time when Abraham received the first promise.
claim: 바울은 갈라디아인 3장에서 율법이 아브라함에게 첫 번째 약속을 받은 시점보다 430년 후에 주어졌다고 가르친다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This preceded the covenant of circumcision by twenty-four years.
claim: 아브라함에게 주어진 첫 번째 약속은 할례의 언약보다 24년 이전에 이루어졌다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This promise, first made with reference to Abraham himself, and afterwards renewed with reference to his seed, is the covenant to which this passage evidently refers.
claim: 아브라함에게 처음으로 주어진 약속은 그의 자손에 대한 약속과 관련하여 갱신되었으며, 이 약속이 성경 본문에서 언급하는 계약이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Hence, believers hold their connection with Abraham receiving the great gospel promise, and not with Abraham receiving the covenant of circumcision; with Abraham as first distinguished by the circumcision of the heart, and not with Abraham as afterwards distinguished by the circumcision of the flesh.
claim: 믿는 이들은 아브라함이 받은 큰 복음의 약속과 관련되어 있으며, 할례의 언약과는 관련되어 있지 않다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Pree cisely the same view is presented in the fourth chapter of Romans, in which it is taught that believers are connected, not with the circumcised, but with the uncircumcised Abraham, in obtaining the blessing of justification.
claim: 믿는 자들은 율법의 외적인 표식인 할례를 받은 아브라함과 연결되지 않고, 오직 복음의 약속을 받은 아브라함과 연결되어 있음을 나타낸다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The judaizing Christians taught, “Except ye be circumcised and keep the law, ye cannot be saved.” This was the current doctrine of the Jews.
claim: 유대화된 기독교인들은 율법을 지키고 할례를 받지 않으면 구원받을 수 없다고 가르쳤다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: They gloried in the covenant of circumcision, and their connection with the circumcised Abraham; and for the purpose of securing a title to the earthly Canaan, literal , descent from Abraham, and the circumcision that is outward in the flesh, were sufficient.
claim: 유다화된 기독교인들은 율법을 지키고 할례를 받는 것이 구원에 필요하다고 가르쳤으며, 아브라함과의 관계와 육신의 외적인 할례를 중요시했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But Paul opposed the doctrine of the judaizing teachers, and opened a different view of the Holy Spirit’s teachings in the Old Testament.
claim: 바울은 유다화하는 교사들의 교리를 반대하며 구약에서 성령의 가르침에 대한 다른 관점을 열어젖혔다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He taught that to secure the spiritual blessings which Abraham enjoyed, we must seek them in the way in which Abraham obtained them.
claim: 아브라함이 받은 영적 축복을 얻기 위해서는 아브라함이 그 축복을 얻은 방법으로 그것들을 추구해야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He did not obtain the favor of God by circumcision and keeping the law; but enjoyed this bless- 174 INFANT MEMBERSHIP.
claim: 아브라함이 하나님의 은혜를 받은 방식은 할례와 율법 지키기 때문이 아님

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He received the blessing by faith; and every one who would be blessed with him, must seek it in this way.
claim: 아브라함은 믿음으로祝福을 받았으며, 그를 통해 祝福을 받고자 하는 모든 사람은 같은 방법으로 그것을 추구해야 한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These arguments of Paul, in which he deduced the true doctrine of the gospel from the Scriptures of the Old Testament, were powerful in opposition to the judaizing theory.
claim: 바울의 논증은 구약 성경에서 복음의 참된 교리를 유추해내는 것이었고, 유대교적 이론에 대한 반박으로 강력했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The covenant of circumcision in its literal sense, included in the covenant seed none but the literal descendants of Abraham.
claim: 할례의 언약은 문자적인 의미에서 아브라함의 실제 자손만을 포함한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The patriarch and his sons were commanded to circumcise all the males of the household, including the servants born in the house, and those bought with money; but these servants did not thereby become incorporated with the covenant seed.
claim: 아브라함의 가계에서 할례를 받은 하인들은 언약의 씨앗과 하나되지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: None of the servants in the families of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, had this privilege conferred on them; and it cannot be supposed that the servants of their descendants were more highly favored than the servants of the patriarchs themselves.
claim: 아브라함, 이삭, 야곱의 가내에서 태어난 종이나 돈으로 산 종들은 할례를 받았지만 언약의 씨앗이 되지 못했다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: On the contrary, those servants, though circumcised, are expressly said in the covenant itself, to be “ not of thy seed.” When the Congregation of the Lord was instituted, provision was made for gentiles to be admitted to the privileges of its worship on conforming to the law of circumcision; but they were nevertheless strangers within the gate, and not a part of the covenant seed, or entitled to a part in the land of Canaan.
claim: 구약의 언약에서 순종과 이방인으로 구분되었으며, 할례를 받은 순종만이 언약의 혜택을 받았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Genealogical records were kept distinguishing the seed proper from the proselytes of the gate; and hence Paul was able to call himself “a Hebrew of the Hebrews ;” that is, a Hebrew by original extraction.
claim: 유대인 기록은 순수한 유대인과 개종자들을 구분하기 위해 유지되었고, 이로 인해 바울은 자신을 '히브리人の 히브리인'이라고 불렀다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: As the covenant of circumcision in its literal sense, admitted none into the covenant seed but literal descendants of Abraham ; so in the allegorical sense, none are included in the spiritual seed but true believers.
claim: 영적 의미에서 아브라함의 영적 후손은 참된 믿음의 사람들만을 포함한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This is clear from many passages of Scripture :— “ So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham. ....If ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.”?
claim: 성경의 여러 구절에 따르면, 믿음으로 말미암은 자들만이 아브라함의 영적 후손으로 간주된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The following passage is perfectly decisive on this subject, and shows conclusively that genuine faith is intended, and not the mere profession of it: “ Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed.” 3
claim: 진정한 믿음은 은혜로 말미암아 약속이 모든 후손에게 확실히 이루어지도록 하기 위해 필요하다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: One among the promises made to Abraham was, “I will make 3f - thee a great nation.” In the covenant of circumcision, it was promised that he should be the father of many nations; and the nation of Israel was contemplated as one of these.
claim: 아브라함에게 약속된 것 중 하나는 그를 큰 민족으로 만들 것이라는 것이었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The covenant in its literal sense, instituted no ecclesia or worshipping congregation.
claim: 아브라함에게 주어진 언약은 교회나 예배 모임을 직적으로 설립하지 않았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: A cahal for the worship of God, was instituted by Moses; and laws and ceremonies for that worship were instituted with it.
claim: 모세는 하나님께 예배를 드리는 회중을 세웠고, 그 예배를 위한 법과 의식도 함께 정했다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The covenant then made with Israel had ordinances of divine service and a worldly sanctuary ; but he who looks for these in the covenant of circumcision will look in vain.
claim: 모세가 세운 언약은 하나님께 대한 예배를 위한 규례와 世俗적인 성소를 포함하고 있었지만, 할례의 언약에서는 이러한 것들을 찾을 수 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It contains no sanctuary, no ordinances of divine worship, no priesthood, no assembly.
claim: 할례의 언약에는 성소나 신적 예배의 규례, 사제직이나 회중이 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: We have shown that the cahal instituted by Moses has been dissolved; and, if the covenant of circumcision still survives, it exists as it did before the days of Moses—a national covenant, made with the literal descendants of Abraham, admitting no others to be incorporated with the covenant seed, and making no provision for the public worship of God.
claim: 모세가 제정한 회중은 해산되었으며, 할례의 언약이 여전히 존재한다면 그것은 모세 이전과 같이 아브라함의 실제 자손들과 맺어진 국적 언약으로서 존재하며, 다른 사람들을 그 언약의 씨앗에 결합시키지 않으며, 하나님의 공적인 예배를 위한 조치를 제공하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Surely, the Christian church is not founded on this covenant.
claim: 기독교 교회는 할례의 언약에 근거하지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Since the covenant of circumcision instituted no ecclesia, and cannot admit gentile infants among the covenant seed, the doctrine of infant church-membership cannot be affected by the question, whether the covenant has been abrogated, or is now in force: and, for any purpose of our present inquiry, we are under no obligation to decide this question.
claim: 할례의 언약은 교회를 세우지 않았으며 이방인 유아들을 언약의 씨앗으로 받아들일 수 없기 때문에, 어린이를 교회 회원으로 받는 교리는 언약이 폐지되었는지 여부에 영향을 받지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Since this covenant existed before that which was made by Moses, the abrogation of the latter may have left the former just as it had previously been.
claim: 모세의 계약이 폐지되어도 이전에 존재했던 계약은 그대로 유지될 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: In it, the land of Canaan was given for an everlasting possession; and the covenant is styled “an everlasting covenant.” We may hence infer, that the covenant will continue in force as long as the Israelites shall possess the land of Canaan.
claim: 가나안 땅은 이스라엘 백성에게 영원한 소유물로 주어졌으며, 이 계약은 "영원한 계약"으로 불리며, 이스라엘 백성이 가나안 땅을 소유하는 한 계약이 효력을 유지할 것이라고 추론할 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If the general expectation be well founded, that they will return to their land and repossess it, the covenant must be still in force.
claim: 이스라엘이 그 땅을 되찾으면 언약이 여전히 효력을 갖는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The facts that, since the abrogation of the Mosaic covenant, they have been called the people of God ;* that they have the promise of being restored again to his favor;* and are declared not to be cast off, because the gifts and calling of God are without repentance ;* confirm this view.
claim: 모세 언약의 폐지 이후에도 이스라엘은 여전히 하나님의 백성으로 불려지고, 그들의 복귀와 관련된 약속이 확인되며, 하나님의 선물과 부르심이 후회 없이 유지됨으로써 언약이 여전히 효력을 가지고 있음을 확신할 수 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: declared converts from among the gentiles to be under no obligation to be circumcised, they did not release Jews from this obligation.
claim: 이방인으로부터 회심한 사람들은 할례를 받을 의무가 없지만 유대인들은 여전히 이 의무를 지닌다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Fora gentile to be circumcised, is an admission that the Congregation of the Lord is still in being, and the Mosaic law still in force; and for any one, whether Jew or gentile, to be circumcised as a means of salvation, is to set aside Christ and render him unprofitable.
claim: 외인에게서 할례를 받는 것은 주님의 회중이 여전히 존재하며 모세의 법이 여전히 시행되고 있음을 인정하는 것이며, 누구든지 유대인이나 외인이 구원이라는 목적으로 할례를 받는 것은 그리스도를 배척하고 그를 무익하게 만드는 것이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But can any one prove that it is inconsistent with the gospel for a Jew to retain circumcision, as a token of his connection with Abraham, and his interest in that remarkable people, through whom he still expects God to display the riches of his grace in the most wonderful manner ?
claim: 유대人が 율법의 상징으로서 할례를 유지하는 것은 복음과 모순되지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Is the covenant of circumcision in force, in its allegorical sense?
claim: 할례의 언약이 비유적인 의미에서 여전히 유효한가?

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The portrait and the man exist independently of each other.
claim: 인물과 초상화는 서로 독립적으로 존재한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If the covenant of circumcision is in force at all, it is in force in that only sense in which it is a covenant— namely, the literal.
claim: 할례의 언약이 유효하다면 그것은 문자적인 의미에서만 유효하다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: No one would say that the ceremonial law is now in force, because the spiritual truths which the ceremonies prefigured abide for ever.
claim: 세례의 의식법은 영원한 영적 진리를 상징하기 때문에 더 이상 시행되지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Whether the covenant is abrogated, or is now in force, the spiritual instruction derived from it is the everlasting gospel.
claim: 성약은 폐지되었거나 현재 시행 중이든 관계없이 성약에서 파생된 영적 교훈은 영원한 복음이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: While the covenant, literally construed, gives no sanction to infant church-membership, the spiritual use which is made of it in the Scriptures incidentally decides that all the members of the primitive churches were believers.
claim: 성경에서 언급하는 교회 회원은 믿는 자들이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Paul says to the Galatians: “ Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.” ee “Ye are all the children of God by faith in Jesus Christ.
claim: 갈라디아 교회 구성원들은 모두 믿는 자들로 간주되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed.” These texts prove that the members of the Galatian churches were all accounted the children of Abraham, in the spiritual sense—that is, were true believers—and what was true of those churches, must have been true of all other churches instituted by the apostles.
claim: 갈라디아 교회 회원들은 영적인 의미에서 아브라함의 자손으로 간주된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: A portrait is not more distinct from the man whom it resembles, nor a shadow more distinct from the substance which casts it, than is the covenant of circumcision from the spiritual truth which it represents, in the allegorical interpretation of it.
claim: 할례의 언약은 그것이 대표하는 영적 진리를 상징하는 것과는 별개이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: infant church-membership. {t follows the literal sense, from Abra- ` ham down to the introduction of the gospel, and accounts the literal seed, during this period, to be the church: it then follows the — spiritual sense, and introduces gentile believers among the covenant seed: it then returns to the law of literal descent, and follows this for one generation, and then abandons it.
claim: 아브라함부터 복음의 도입까지는 문자적인 의미를 따르며, 이 기간 동안 문자적인 씨를 교회로 간주하고, 영적 의미를 따른다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: By this unaccountable mixture of interpretations, the immediate literal descendants of those who are, or ought to be, according to their profession, the Spiritual seed of Abraham, are supposed to be brought within the covenant, and incorporated with the eovenant seed: but, alas! they are a seed which inherit neither the literal nor the spiritual promises made to the patriarch.
claim: 아브라함의 영적 후손의 직계 자녀들은 언약에 포함되지만, 아브라함에게 약속된 물리적이나 영적인 약속을 상속받지 않는다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: They do not inherit the literal promises, because they are gentiles ; nor the spiritual promises, because these are secured only to believers.
claim: 아브라함의 영적 후손의 직계 자손은 육적인 약속도 영적인 약속도 물려받지 못한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The word which is here rendered “ children,” denotes posterity, immediate or remote, without respect to age.
claim: 성경에서 '자녀'라는 단어는 나이와 상관없이 직계나 방계를 막론하고 후손을 의미한다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The promise here referred to appears, from the words which immediately precede, to be the promise of the Holy Spirit; but, whether it be this, or the promise made to Abraham as the argument supposes, it must be understood to include spiritual blessings.
claim: 성령의 약속이나 아브라함에게 주어진 약속은 영적 축복을 포함한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Three classes of persons are mentioned, to whom the promise is given; the Israelites of that generation, their posterity, and the gentiles: “you, your children, and all that are afar off.” To neither of these classes is the promise given without condition or limitation.
claim: 성령의 약속이나 아브라함에게 하신 약속과 같은 하나님의 약속은 영적 축복을 포함하며, 이 약속은 이스라엘인, 그들의 자손, 그리고 모든 먼 곳에 있는 사람들에게 조건과 제한이 따라서 주어진다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When it is said, “Repent, for the promise is to you,” the receiving of the promise is evidently suspended on the condition of repentance.
claim: 약속을 받는 것은 회개의 조건에 따라 결정된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This is fully established by the limiting clause, “even as many as the Lord our God shall call.” The promise is not absolute to all who are externally called by the
claim: 주님의 부르심에 따라 선택된 자들에게만 약속이 주어짐을 한정하는 절 "주 우리 하나님이 부르시는 많은 사람들"에 의해 완전히 확립된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: gospel, but to those only who are effectually called to repentance.
claim: 복음은 효과적으로 회개에 부름받은 사람들에게만 적용된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Though the word “ children” may sometimes be used with exclusive application to infants, there is no reason to suppose that such use of it is made here, but the whole posterity are intended; and it cannot be that spiritual blessings were promised to all those, without condition or limitation.
claim: 성경에서 '자녀들'이라는 단어가 사용될 때는 때때로 영적 축복을 받은 모든 사람에게 조건이나 제한 없이 약속된 것으로 이해할 수 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Peter had charged them with the crime of crucifying the Lord Jesus.
claim: 베드로는 그들에게 주 예수를 십자가에 못 박은 죄를 고한 바 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: When this crime was committed, in calling on Pilate to crucify him, they had said: “ His blood be on us, and on our children.” This fact rendered the information suitable and welcome, that the same means of salvation that were granted to them, would be granted to their posterity.
claim: 유대인들이 예수를 십자가에 못 박은 죄를 지었을 때, 그들은 자손에게도 그 죄의 책임이 미치도록 할 것이라고 말했으며, 이 사실로 인해 그들에게 주어진 구원의 수단이 그들의 자손에게도 주어질 것이라는 정보가 적절하고 환영받을 수 있게 되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: “ The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.’”?
claim: 하나님의 나라가 너희에게서 빼앗기고 그 열매를 맺는 민족에게 주어질 것이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The name of a type is sometimes applied to the thing typified.
claim: 유형의 이름은 때때로 유형화된 것에 적용된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Regeneration is called circumcision; but, to show that literal circumcision is not intended, it is called the circumcision of the heart, or the circumcision of Christ.
claim: 성경에서 재생을 상징하는 순종은 마음의 순종이나 그리스도의 순종으로 불리운다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Heaven is called a country, in allusion to the country promised to Abraham, which typified it; but, for the sake of distinction, the epithets ‘ better” and “ heavenly’’ are applied: ‘‘a better country, that is, a heavenly.” The nation of Israel, marked by the literal circumcision, and heirs of the earthly Canaan, typified those who are circumcised in heart, and are heirs of the heavenly country.
claim: 하늘나라가 아브라함에게 약속된 땅을 상징하며, 마음의 할례를 받은 자들이 하늘나라의 유업을 얻는다고 함

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These last are on this account called a nation; but, to distinguish them from the nation which typified them, they are called “a nation bringing forth the fruits” of the kingdom; that is, the fruits of holy obedience to God as their king.
claim: 성도들은 하나님께 대한 거룩한 순종의 열매를 맺는 민족으로서 구별된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Peter calls them “a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar people.” They are not a nation, in the literal sense of the term, as the nation of Israel was.
claim: 신자들은 선택받은 세대, 왕 같은 제사장, 거룩한 민족, 특별한 백성으로 불린다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Earthly nations included infants, but this spiritual nation consists of those who bring forth the fruits of the kingdom; and who, according to Peter, “show forth the praises of him who hath called them out of darkness into his marvellous light.” These things cannot be predicated of infants.
claim: 영적 국가의 구성원은 왕국을 위한 열매를 맺으며 어둠에서 빛으로 불러낸 자의 영광을 선포하는 사람들이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: It follows, therefore, that, in this transfer of the kingdom, infants are not its recipients.
claim: 영적 왕국은 영적인 열매를 맺는 자들로 구성되며,嬰兒들은 이 王國의 受託者가 아니다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The government of that nation has been called a theocracy.
claim: 이스라엘의 정부는 신정정치체제로 불린다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: God was their king; and various benefits resulted to them from being under his reign.
claim: 하나님은 그들의 왕이었고, 그의 통치 아래 있기 때문에 여러 가지 혜택이 그들에게 돌아갔다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: To these benefits the text may refer ; and the sense may be, that the peculiar privilege of having God to reign over them, should no longer distinguish them from other nations of the earth; but this privilege would henceforth be confined to a spiritual people, to be selected out of all nations.
claim: 하나님의 특권은 더 이상 한 민족에게만 국한되지 않고 영적 백성들에게로 확장된다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: But, as the phrase, “ kingdom of God,” was commonly used by Christ to denote the new kingdom which he was establishing, the reference may be exclusively to this.
claim: 그리스도께서 세우신 새로운 왕국을 가리키는 "하나님의 나라"라는 용어가 사용되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He was born “King of the Jews,” and was crucified with this title.
claim: 예수는 유대인의 왕으로 태어났으며 이 칭호와 함께 십자가에 못 박혔다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He was sent, as he himself declared, not to the gentiles, but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
claim: 예수는 유대인에게 보내심을 받았다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The first proclamation of his reign was made to this people; and the beginning and first benefits of his reign were confined to them.
claim: 그리스도의 첫 번째 선포는 이스라엘 집의 잃어버린 양에게 이루어졌으며, 그의 통치의 시작과 첫 번째 혜택은 그들에게 국한되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Their rejection of his reign was made the occasion of its extension to the gentiles: “It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the gentiles.”" The blessings of the Messiah’s reign were expected by the nation to be theirs, and the first offer and bestowment of them accorded with this expectation: but the peculiar privilege was taken from them when they rejected their king; and it is now enjoyed by those who obey him in every nation.
claim: 유대인들이 메시아의 통치를 거부한 것이 외인에게 그것을 확장시키는 계기가 되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These, and these only, bring forth the fruits of the kingdom; and, however the transfer to them may be understood, it cannot prove the churchmembership of infants.
claim: 유아들의 교회 회원資格은 왕국을 위한 열매를 맺는 것과 관련이 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The last Scripture cited in the argument has been much relied on, as proof that the Christian church is a continuation of an organized society which existed in the Old Testament dispensation.
claim: 기독교 교회는 구약 시대에 존재했던 조직화된 사회의 연장이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Under the figure of the good olive-tree, Paul is supposed to teach that the church sprang from Abraham, and that it has continued to the present time.
claim: 바울은 좋은 올리브 나무의 비유를 통해 교회가 아브라함으로부터 시작되었고 현재까지 계속되었다는 것을 가르친다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: the natural branches were broken off.
claim: 자연의 가지들은 끊어졌습니다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The reason for their separation is expressly given: “ Because of unbelief, they were broken off.” Since the unbelieving branches were taken away by this act, none were left but believing branches.
claim: 불신앙 때문에 이스라엘의 일부가 끊어졌고, 믿는 가지들만 남게 되었다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These are the remnant before spoken of; “the remnant according to the election of grace: the seed intended when it is said, “ Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.” 1
claim: 선택의 은혜에 따라 남은 자는 믿음의 잔류민이다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The character of these branches is made known by the words with which Paul addresses them: “ Thou standest by faith.” We are hence assured that these also were believing branches.
claim: 믿음으로 서 있는 믿는 가지들

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: This accords with what is elsewhere taught: « That the blessing of Abraham might come on the gentiles through faith.”
claim: 아브라함의 축복이 이방인에게 믿음을 통해 임한다

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: Another important change is still expected when the natural branches which were broken off shall be “ graffed in again.” The condition on which it will be done is expressly stated : “ They also
claim: 자연의 가지들이 다시嫁接될 때 또 다른 중요한 변화가 예상된다.
citations: 1. The olive-tree underwent an important change when many of

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: If they come in again, they must come as believing branches.
claim: 믿음의 가지로 다시 들어오지 않는 이상 그들은 회복될 수 없다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: These three comprehend all the changes which the olive-tree is said to undergo; and as a consequence of these, none but belieying branches have a present, or can have a future connection with the tree.
claim: 올리브 나무에 대한 비유는 믿음의 가지들만이 현재나 미래에 나무와 연결될 수 있음을 보여준다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The design for which this figurative illustration was introduced, and the explanations which accompany it, clearly show that the natural branches were designed to represent the natural seed of Abraham; and the changes which the tree undergoes, are precisely such as substituted the spiritual seed for the natural, the children by faith for the children according to the flesh.
claim: 올리브 나무의 비유는 영적 후손이 자연적 후손을 대체하는 것을 나타낸다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The whole scope of the apostle’s teaching in connection with the passage, if attentively considered, leaves no reasonable doubt that this was the design of the figure.
claim: 사도 바울의 가르침에 따르면 올리브 나무 비유는 자연적인 아브라함의 자손과 영적 아브라함의 자손을 대신하는 것을 나타낸다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: He who seeks to extend the likeness beyond its proper limit, is in danger of mistake.
claim: 유사성을 그 적절한 한계를 넘어서 확장하려고 하는 사람은 오류에 빠질 위험이 있다.

author: John L. Dagg
source_text: The chief question before the apostle’s mind, related to the branches; and what these signify he has sufficiently informed us.
claim: 사도는 올리브나무의 가지를 강조하였으며, 그 의미에 대해 충분히 설명하였다.

author: John L. Dagg
